newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to continue rapid growth in Q1 - CSS analyst.
newsitem.headline: Poland to continue rapid growth in Q1 - CSS analyst.

text.p: Poland's rapid economic growth would likely continue in the first quarter of 1997, said Tadeusz Chroscicki, chief analyst at the Government's Centre for Strategic Studies (CSS), in his macroeconomic forecast.

Chroscicki said industrial output growth in the first quarter may top 10 percent, after 10.1 percent growth year-on-year in December 1996, and will continue to be fuelled by domestic consumer and investment demand.
The forecast, submitted monthly to Reuters, also said inflation would likely be between 2.7 and three percent in January and 1.8 percent in February after December's 1.3 percent rise.
He expected year-on-year inflation to fall to 18 percent in March from 18.5 percent last December.
Chroscicki said month-on-month inflation should ease to between 0.9 and one percent after the first quarter.

He said Poland would have a $3 billion current account trade deficit in the first quarter of 1997, after an estimated $8.1 shortfall in all of 1996, which would keep Polish currency reserves basically flat in the January-March period.
